thread:
alex: seeing node_exporter and dcgm-exporter restart loops on a subset of GPU nodes after the kernel hotpatch yesterday. lots of OOMKilled in kubelet logs. anyone else?
priya: yup saw spikes, pods went CrashLoopBackOff on ~6 nodes, readiness probes failing. startup time seems variable (5-12s).
miriam: logs point to OOMs during container startup. snippet from kubelet: 
```E1122 10:23:45 container_manager.go:123] killing container "dcgm-exporter": OOMKilled (memory cgroup exceeded)
```
sam: my initial hunch: liveness probe is too aggressive + no graceful shutdown handling in the exporter. liveness set to 5s / failureThreshold 3 in current daemonset, so kubelet kills before exporter finishes init/flush.
jake: can we try relaxing probes & add preStop? proposed change: 
```yaml
livenessProbe:
  httpGet: 
    path: /metrics
    port: 9100
  initialDelaySeconds: 15
  periodSeconds: 30
  failureThreshold: 5
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /health
    port: 9100
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 10
terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60
lifecycle:
  preStop:
    exec:
      command: ["/bin/sh","-c","sleep 10"]
```
priya: +1 to that. also the exporter has a heavy NVML init on some older drivers; moving any non-critical caching into postStart might lower startup memory spike.
infra-bot: rolling update initiated for daemonset gpu-metrics-exporter with canary=10% (job id: roll-1987654321).
alex: noticed on a few older nodes node_exporter hit fd limits which made the process unstable under scrape bursts. patching systemd ulimit for node-exporter fixed one node in repro.
miriam: since this is a daemonset, we should set updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable to 1 to avoid mass churn: 
```yaml
updateStrategy:
  rollingUpdate:
    maxUnavailable: 1
  type: RollingUpdate
```
sam: important: during the rollout we will lose metrics for short windows - tune Prometheus alerts to avoid pager fatigue. silence exporter_down alerts for 2m when release=r2 matches. rule snippet: 
```yaml
- alert: ExporterTemporarilyUnavailable
  expr: absent(up{job=~"gpu-metrics.*",release="r2"}) and time() - changes(up{job=~"gpu-metrics.*",release="r2"}) < 120
  for: 2m
```
jake: also thinking about capacity: cordon nodes needing the patch and move critical inference pods to nodes with more headroom. we can apply a temporary taint gpu-rollout=true:NoSchedule and a toleration for the metrics canary pods.
priya: agree. i'll add a small runbook: 1) apply probe/termination patch in staging canary 10% 2) watch grafana gpu/exporter-up and cluster-autoscaler events for 10m 3) if stable, proceed with maxUnavailable=1 rollout 4) if repeated OOMs, escalate to infra-ml to repro on a spare node and capture `pmap`/`smaps`.
alex: can someone open the PR and include changelog + test plan? also add a note to the SLO dashboard about temporary expected missing series during daemonset upgrades so oncall isn't surprised.
jake: opening PR now: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge_requests/6421 : will include probe + lifecycle + updateStrategy + Prometheus alert tweak.
priya: i'll monitor the canary tonight and leave a comment in the PR with grafana links. thanks all.
alex: thanks — ping here if any flaps. :)
